findings.description: F0023-R1-001 remains unresolved. Nullable derivative presence is treated as optional regardless of frame_indices. There is no PilotSubmission attachment branch requiring the derivative, validating selected indices or establishing attachment correspondence. An isolated execution of the actual preparation and reader functions returned a usable E3 context with no diagnostics for frame_indices=[0] and derivative=null through both direct and SQLite-reader paths. PilotSubmission.human_record and pilot admission explicitly require the derivative for frame attachments.

F0023-R1-002 remains unresolved. BindingContext preparation checks FirstView presence and time but never compares its content identity with the binding. A correctly pinned FirstView for different content can supply chronology when its timestamp matches. Traversing its media and registration references does not establish their relationship to this binding. The existing generation.validate_admission check rejects this mismatch.

F0023-R1-004 remains unresolved despite the new timestamp controls. Several rejection guards still lack isolated negative tests, including binding seal intent mismatch, binding origin anchors mismatch and run link context mismatch. Removing those guards would not alter the current targeted expectations. The inventory assertion covers only selected paths, while its uniqueness check is tautological because production inventory() already builds a set. Boundary-call observations cover only dimension and coverage. Most rejection assertions also do not identify the exact expected subject. These tests cannot establish that every declared prerequisite is necessary and checked.
